XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT The P.I., of K.R.Puram Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 4 for C.C.No.53622/2018 the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A, 504,
506 R/ w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, she got married with accused No.1 on 31.08.2007 as per Hindu rites and customs at Corporation Hall, Halasuru Tank Road, in the presence of the elders, at the time of marriage as per the say of the accused No.1 to 4, the parents of the CW.1 have given Necklace, Earrings, Ring for CW.1 and one chain, two rings and one watch to the accused No.1 as dowry.

It is further alleged that, the complainant went to her matrimonial house at No.32, North Avenue, ITI Colony, Bengaluru and led happy marital life for one month and thereafter, the accused persons subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally.

It is further alleged that, the accused has the habit of betting and he assaulted CW.1 for more dowry and the parents of CW.1 gave total amount of Rs.1,47,000/- on different dates and accused No.2 to 4 abused her in filthy language and subjected her to cruelty by harassing both physically and mentally.

It is further alleged that, on 24.08.2014 at about 9.00 PM, accused No.1 picked up quarrel with CW.1 infront of parental house of CW.1 and twisted the C.C.No.53622/2018 hand of CW.1 and threatened her with dire consequences for more dowry.

Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1, CW.10 has registered the case against accused No.1 to 3 in P.S. Crime No.351/2014 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a), 504,
506 R/w 34 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Investigating Officers/ CW.10 to 12 after completion of the investigation, CW.12 has submitted final report against the accused No.1 to 4 for the above said offences.

3. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offence alleged against the accused No.1 to 4 and registered the criminal case against them.
4. After registration of the case, the accused No.1 has appeared before this court and enlarged on bail, the accused No.2 to 4 have appeared and were enlarged on bail.
Copies of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to them in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused No.1 and 4 only.
They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

In order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4, the prosecution has examined one witness out of 12 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.07 and closed its side.
In lieu of absence of incriminating circumstances appearing against accused No.1 to 4, recording of their statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.
6. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all in furtherance of common intention have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 R/w 34 of IPC ?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all has demanded more dowry from CW.1 and subjected her to cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?
5. What Order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 to 4 : In the Negative.
 Point No.5 : As per the final order  for the following;
Rani vs Ramachandran on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158154707/
3  C.C.No.53622/2018  REASONS  9. POINT Nos.1 to 4 :-
As these four points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repeti- tion of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4, the prosecution has examined the complainant/victim/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and relied upon seven documents.
10.

sentences.text: In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4, the prosecution has examined the complainant / victim CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, the said witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned APP appearing for the State with permission treated the said witness as hostile and fully cross examined her, wherein, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 in order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4.
11.

On perusal of the materials on record and the oral & documentary evidence of P.W.1, she has categorically admitted that, she has compromised the matter with the accused Nos.1 to 4 and she is leading happy marital life with C.C.No.53622/2018 accused No.1.

In view of the evidence of P.W.1,
since the matter was compromised, the prayer of the learned Senior Asst. Public Prosecutor for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses was rejected as no purpose would be served.
As the P.W.1 has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution, the evidence on record is not at all helpful to substantiate the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4.
Hence, there is no cogent and convincing evidence against the accused No.1 to 4.
Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused No.1 to 4 and hence, the Point Nos.1 to 4 are answered in the "Negative".

12. Point No.5 :- In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The Bail bonds of the accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force for the period C.C.No.53622/2018 of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 08 th day of May, 2025.)
